The coordinator assigned **v452/v451** to #8899. For #8900, it is checking whether the new read key could leave existing stored receipts unprotected. I'll set the pair and commit #8899's merge.

#8899 has its new pair. **v452/v451** is set in merge commit `3ab5f1a279`, together with the epoch token, its comment and its component row. Its post-merge compile check and focused tests are running in the background. Then I'll recheck master and the ready PRs numerically and send the coordinator the head.

The reviewer accepted the combined-tree check and has no objection to closing out both PRs.

**#8900 waits on the coordinator,** which is checking whether recording the selected mount's file version could leave older stored receipts unprotected. I sent it the reviewer's statement that the key matches the old key exactly. I also sent my own reasoning, which isn't verified: before this PR, the nested pooled read already recorded the file's live version, so a receipt could only differ if the live version and the selected mount's version ever differ for a ready selection. I don't have evidence either way, so #8900 stays a draft until the coordinator confirms.

Background runs:
- **#8900:** post-merge checks on `56599e3f31`.
- **#8899:** post-merge checks on `3ab5f1a279`.

The coordinator ruled that #8900 also needs identity changes, as a conservative step:
- ICFG pair **v470/v469**;
- token `-8884-rust-selected-import-reads`, with its comment and component row.

The reason is the intended change of authority, from live, pooled imports to the operation's selected imports. Nobody has shown a stale unit. I'll check whether #8900's background build is finished before editing that lane.
#8900's post-merge checks all pass: compile check, lib 410/410, policy regressions 4/4, operation tests 111/111. I'll make its identity edits.
The diff is what the coordinator assigned. I'll commit it and run only the identity tests and fmt, as the coordinator directed for a change that only touches identity values.
While I wait, I'll merge master into #8900. Its pair is above master, but the identity lines will probably conflict.

#8900 has its identity values and the latest master merged:
- `04ecc05916` sets v470/v469 and adds the `-8884-rust-selected-import-reads` token with its comment and component row. The identity tests pass (29/29) and fmt is clean.
- `0438c593c1` merges master again, resolved with a small reusable script, `/tmp/mrbox-bugs/tools/resolve_identity.py`. The script keeps both sides' comments and our literal, appends our token to master's epoch string, keeps both sides' component rows, and checks the result.
- The PR body no longer says "no identity lever". Its identity section now states the coordinator's ruling in its own terms: the old reader already recorded the live-OID key, the nested reads were real and checked, no stale unit was reproduced, and the rotation is a conservative response to the change of read authority.
- A compile check, the identity tests and focused tests are running in the background on the merge.

**#8899 is blocked again.** Master reached v462/v461, above its v452/v451, so I've asked the coordinator for a new pair. Master is moving quickly. To avoid another round, as soon as the pair arrives I'll set it, merge, run the identity tests, push and mark ready in one sequence.

The coordinator assigned **v474/v473** to #8899 and said not to merge master again just because it moved. A change that only touches identity values needs only an identity commit plus the reviewer's check. I'll make that commit on #8899's current head, `3ab5f1a279`.
The identity commit is `c461969a67`, and its identity tests pass (29/29). I'll push #8899 and update the pair in its PR body.

Both PRs are pushed with their final identity values, and the PR heads match:

| PR | Head | ICFG pair | Epoch token |
|---|---|---|---|
| #8899 (#8866) | `c461969a67` | v474/v473 | `-8866-rust-unwrapped-receiver` |
| #8900 (#8884) | `0438c593c1` | v470/v469 | `-8884-rust-selected-import-reads` |

- **Numeric check:** master is now v463/v462, below both pairs. The highest ready in-flight pair I found is v443.
- **Since the reviewer cleared each source head,** the branches have only master merges whose conflicts were identity lines, resolved by the repo rule, plus identity-only commits. Following the coordinator's instruction, I won't merge master again just because it moves.
- **Latest checks:** compile checks pass, identity tests pass 29/29 on both, and #8900's two regressions pass 2/2. #8899's last full run was lib 410/410 and effects golden 22/22.

I've sent the final heads and those details to the reviewer and the coordinator. I'll mark both PRs ready once the reviewer replies, unless either objects.
The reviewer approved both final heads, with no conditions left. I'll confirm the heads one more time and mark both ready.
Both are marked ready, with the API heads and remote heads matching the reviewed heads. I'll remove the throwaway scratch worktree. No child was started in it.

Both PRs are ready for the merge queue. The reviewer approved both final heads with no conditions left, and the coordinator assigned their identity values.

- **#8899 (for #8866):** Rust method calls whose receiver comes from `?`, `.unwrap()` or `.expect(..)` on a std `Option` or `Result` now bind to the pack's model of the method. Before, only calls on parameters and annotated locals bound. Head `c461969a67`, ICFG pair v474/v473, token `-8866-rust-unwrapped-receiver`.
- **#8900 (for #8884):** the Rust import reads under a selected resolution operation now go through that operation, and they record which file version they read. Head `0438c593c1`, ICFG pair v470/v469, token `-8884-rust-selected-import-reads`.

Review found four real problems, all fixed:
- **Crash on a bare `Result`:** an unwrap of a modeled `Result` with no type arguments crashed the query.
- **Lost reference:** `Option<&File>` lost its `&` before reaching the trait checks.
- **Second operation:** the type reader opened a second resolution operation inside the first one.
- **Missing read record:** #8900 at first dropped the record of which file version was read.

Each fix has a `#[hardwon]` test that was shown failing before the fix. The last full runs passed:
- the Rust analysis lib (410 tests);
- the effects golden;
- the policy and composition goldens;
- `golden_resolution_facts`;
- the store engine tests;
- a combined run of both branches merged together.

Things to know:
- **#8884 and #8866 stay open.** Neither PR closes its issue. #8884 waits on #8893, the remaining reads that bypass the operation in trait applicability; I filed it and haven't started it.
- **Cost rules still need pack content.** Rust cost rules also need std declarations with self forms (`File` and similar types) in `bifrost-packs`. I haven't filed that yet; it's noted on #8866.
- **#8900's identity change is a precaution.** No stale result was reproduced. The coordinator chose to rotate because the source of the import reads changed.
- **Next step for cost rules:** once both PRs land, rerun the trial in `/tmp/mrbox-bugs/cost-spike/` with a declaration pack. That will show how many of the six cost fixes the rules catch.

I've left the two lane worktrees and their parked children in place, because the PR comments cite their report directories.

The coordinator has no objection to ready, and its reply arrived after I'd already marked both ready. It asked that the combined-tree validation be recorded in the PR evidence, and it isn't yet. I'll add it to both PRs.

#8899 has landed on master. So Rust method calls on values from `?`, `.unwrap()` and `.expect(..)` on std `Option`/`Result` now bind to a pack's model of the method. #8900 is still in the merge queue.

The new issue #8927 is about JVM overlay inputs. It looks related in theme, since it's another case of a dirty state being skipped without a record, but it isn't in either PR's code, so I'm leaving it alone.

I'm keeping the #8866 lane worktree for now. Its parked implementer was started in that directory, and the PR comments cite that child's report directory.

Still open from this work:
- **#8893:** the remaining store reads that bypass the selected operation in trait applicability. #8884 can't close until it lands. Not started.
- **Std declarations in `bifrost-packs`:** declarations with self forms for `File` and similar types, which the cost rules need. Not filed yet.
- **Rerunning the cost-rule trial** with a declaration pack, once #8900 lands too.

Both PRs have landed. The next step, which I said I'd take once both landed, is to rerun the cost-rule trial on current master, now with a std declaration pack. That shows whether the engine work pays off on the six real cost fixes, and which std declarations `bifrost-packs` needs. The trial child is parked with full context, so I'll give it the rerun.

Both #8899 and #8900 are on master. I've sent the cost-rule trial child its second round, on current master:

1. **Build:** a fresh measure-profile CLI from current master.
2. **Pack:** add declaration facts to the trial pack, in the same shape as the landed golden fixture: the `std` crate root, self forms, `File::create` returning `Result<File, io::Error>`, and the `Option`/`Result` types. They cover every type whose methods the six cost fixes call: `File`, the tokio runtime builder, the named-pipe options, the `std::fs` functions and `Command`.
3. **Control:** prove binding works on a control workspace first.
4. **Rerun:** the three rules on the 12 parent/fix pairs and on mr-boxington's current code, with a 15-row noise sample.
5. **Diagnosis:** for every call that still doesn't bind, the exact reason, grouped into missing pack declarations (content for `bifrost-packs`) and engine gaps.

The report goes to `/tmp/mrbox-bugs/cost-spike/round2/REPORT.md`. Its results will decide what to file next: a `bifrost-packs` issue listing the std declarations Rust cost rules need, and possibly more engine issues. Separately, #8893, the remaining reads that bypass the operation, is still open and unstarted.

Two things came in. First, #8948 says my #8899 broke `cargo clippy` on master: `only_used_in_recursion` in `trait_applicability.rs`. A fix PR, #8955, already exists. Master breakage is the responsibility of whoever caused it, so I'll check #8955's state first.
No issue matches, though #2508 (effect summary caching) is related. I'll check whether mr-boxington is public, which decides how the issue can name the reproduction.
mr-boxington is public (`jdx/mr-boxington`), so the issue can give an exact reproduction.
My work on #8866 and #8884 is done for now, so I'll take the in-progress label and my assignment off both.

The second trial still caught **0 of 12** cost fixes with rules over every call in the workspace. The binding fixes work now; the new blocker is that these queries don't finish.

**What the trial showed, on master `849fd2476d` with a std declaration pack:**
- **Binding works.** All four `File::sync_all` forms bind with exhaustive coverage, and `Command.output()` binds in a real historical tree.
- **Queries limited to one file work.** They find the effect at the target site in 3 of 12 fixes (`6abf99836b`, `43cea5bf70`, `a5eefbba21`).
- **Queries over every call never finish.** All 50 effect runs stopped on a budget, even on the 6abf parent tree, which has only 15 Rust files and about 12,000 lines. That run used 36,481 event rows against a limit of 29,959. With `--workspace-scaled-limits` it timed out at 180 s.
- **Noise is still high.** The fallback rule that matches call names gives 977 findings on current code. A 15-row sample had no real bugs and 6 false positives (40%).

**Filed:**
- **#8962:** whole-workspace `call-effects` runs out of budget on a 12k-line workspace. This is now the main blocker, with an exact reproduction on the public `jdx/mr-boxington`.
- **#8964:** a call whose callee resolved but has no summary is reported as `dispatch_unresolved`. The diagnostic says resolved, so rule authors can't tell the two apart.
- **BrokkAi/bifrost-packs#208:** the std declarations with self forms that Rust effect rules need (`File`, `OpenOptions`, `std::fs`, `Command`, the tokio runtime and named pipes, `Option`/`Result`), using the landed test fixture as the template.
- **A round-2 summary on #8866.** I took the in-progress label and my assignment off #8866 and #8884.

**Two smaller findings I didn't file:**
- One unresolved `sync_all` in a real tree binds when I reproduce the same code in isolation. It depends on something else in that tree, so it stays unfiled until I can reduce it.
- Several fixes change how often a call runs, not whether it exists. A rule that only checks "this call is inside a loop" can't see that.

**One mistake of mine:** #8899 broke master's clippy (#8948), and another session fixed it in #8955, already merged. The implementer ran clippy without `-D warnings` and reported "passed" while its log held the warning, and I passed that on without reading the log. I've saved a note to always check clippy logs for warnings before relaying a pass.

**What I'd do next:** fix #8962, or at least profile it to find which step produces the rows. Until it's fixed, no rule built on declared effects over a whole workspace can run, for cost or anything else. #8893 is also still open and not started. I haven't started either; tell me if you want me to take one.
